children.title: Peircean Semiotics and Habit Formation in Intelligent Systems

detail.title: Peircean Semiotics and Habit Formation in Intelligent Systems
detail.summary: An examination of how Peirce's framework of inquiry, abduction, and sign interpretation conceptualizes the emergence of stable interpretive tendencies analogous to preferences.
detail.reason: Synthesizing the collected philosophical framework to address the project question.

children.title: Habit Formation and Convention Emergence in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

detail.title: Habit Formation and Convention Emergence in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
detail.summary: Demonstrates that complex, large-scale conventions and stable preference patterns can emerge from model-free multi-agent reinforcement learning mechanisms, offering a computational counterpart to philosophical habit formation.
detail.reason: Revising notebook nb-emergent-prefs-01 with newly collected computational evidence on model-free reinforcement learning.

children.title: Metareasoning and Self-Correction in Intelligent Systems

detail.title: Metareasoning and Self-Correction in Intelligent Systems
detail.summary: Examines how intelligent systems might identify and revise foundational assumptions through structured metareasoning architectures.
detail.reason: Synthesizes initial perspectives on explainable and pragmatic artificial intelligence frameworks relevant to self-correction.
